data.title: UK Government Borrowed More in October, But Is on Track for Smaller Deficit
data.description:
By Paul Hannon

The U.K. government borrowed more in October than a year earlier, but it remained on course to reduce its budget deficit in the current fiscal year.

The Office for National Statistics on Friday said government spending exceeded its revenues by 17 billion pounds in October, an increase of 800 million pounds from the same month of 2025.

Over the first seven months of the fiscal year that will end in early April, borrowing was 111.3 billion pounds, down 7.3 billion pounds from the same period a year earlier.

At 3.5% of gross domestic product, the budget deficit for the fiscal year to October was lower than the 3.8% recorded a year earlier.

The government's total debt stood at 3.1 trillion pounds, or 95.8% of GDP, up from 93.9% in October 2025.

Write to Paul Hannon at paul.hannon@wsj.com

THE PERFECT CRIME WAS MAKING SURE NOBODY SAW ONE.

THE PERFECT CRIME WAS MAKING SURE NOBODY SAW ONE.

PR Newswire

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 20, 2026

New Las Vegas Book Reveals the Extraordinary Story of a Magician, a Million-Dollar Gambler, and the Casinos That Never Saw Him Coming

Advance Orders Now Open for ROSENBLATT — Coming January 15, 2027

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Las Vegas has produced its share of legendary gamblers, con men, hustlers, and thieves. But few stories are quite like ROSENBLATT, a provocative new book about a man who went from having almost nothing to becoming one of the highest-stakes gamblers in Las Vegas history — without ever risking a dollar of his own money.

He robbed casinos without a gun. He became a million-dollar player. He was eventually barred from virtually every casino in town.

And for years, nobody knew exactly what he had done.

The casinos knew they'd been hit. They never learned how much. They never learned when, and they never learned how.

At the center of the story is Darryl Rosenblatt, a magician whose greatest illusion wasn't performed on a stage. It was performed in plain sight, under the watchful eyes of casino executives, surveillance operators, and some of the most sophisticated security systems in the world.

What began as a remarkable talent for deception became a life of enormous wagers, extraordinary characters, spectacular excess, and ultimately, prison.

But ROSENBLATT is far more than a story about stealing from casinos.

It is the story of an unlikely rise through the underbelly of American life, where survival demanded ingenuity, rules were negotiable, and the difference between a magician and a criminal sometimes depended on who was watching.

Written with biting humor, unapologetic candor, and an insider's knowledge of a Las Vegas most visitors will never see, ROSENBLATT takes readers on a roller coaster ride through three decades of Vegas depravity through the rapier lens of a damaged man.

There are no fictional masterminds here. No Hollywood heists. No masked men running through casino floors with bags of cash.

The theft was the illusion.

And the casinos were the audience.

"Everything in his life had been preparing him for Las Vegas. Las Vegas was not prepared for him."

Scheduled for release January 15, 2027, ROSENBLATT is now available for advance purchase ahead of its official publication.

For readers fascinated by the hidden history of Las Vegas, high-stakes gambling, organized deception, and extraordinary true-life characters, this is a story that challenges everything they think they know about the casino business.

He didn't hide the money. He hid the Crime.

And now, for the first time, he's telling the story.

data.title: Sigenergy Earns Double BloombergNEF Tier 1 Recognition for Power Inverters and Energy Storage in Q4 2026
data.description:
SHANGHAI, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sigenergy, a global innovator in next-generation energy storage solutions, has been officially named a BloombergNEF (BNEF) Tier 1 Manufacturer across both Power Inverters and Energy Storage for the fourth quarter of 2026.


BloombergNEF’s Tier 1 list is widely regarded as one of the renewable energy sector’s most stringent independent benchmarks. Earning dual Tier 1 status in two core categories simultaneously underscores Sigenergy’s strong financial stability, rigorous manufacturing quality, and proven project track record across international markets.

The double recognition validates the real-world reliability of Sigenergy's AI-driven innovative architectures and reflects the growing global adoption of Sigenergy’s core technological strengths:

End-to-End Innovation: Innovative hardware and software integration delivers smarter, safer, and more resilient energy management.
Full-Scenario Scale: Proven field performance spanning residential systems, commercial & industrial (C&I) facilities, and complex utility-scale power plants.
Global Service & Support: Backed by continuous R&D investment and an expanding worldwide service and partner network.

Looking ahead, Sigenergy will continue expanding its global footprint and advancing practical, AI-native energy technologies to support partners, installers, and communities around the world.

About Sigenergy
Founded in 2022 and headquartered in Shanghai, Sigenergy (6656.HK) is a technology-driven company focused on innovation in the new energy sector. Leveraging advanced digital intelligence and a highly skilled talent base, the company has expanded across photovoltaic(PV)generation, smart energy storage and high-efficiency electric vehicle (EV) charging solutions.

Guided by its “AI in All” strategy, Sigenergy integrates artificial intelligence across its product ecosystem to deliver safer, smarter and more efficient energy solutions for households and businesses worldwide.

For more information, visit: www.sigenergy.com

data.title: GenSight Biologics Announces Successful EUR 1.1 Million Fundraising Supported by Existing Shareholders
data.description:
GenSight Biologics Announces Successful EUR 1.1 Million Fundraising Supported by Existing Shareholders

Regulatory News:

NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION, DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY, IN THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, CANADA, AUSTRALIA, JAPAN AND SOUTH AFRICA

GenSight Biologics ("GenSight" or the "Company") (Euronext: SIGHT, ISIN: FR0013183985, PEA-PME eligible), a biopharma company focused on developing and commercializing innovative gene therapies for retinal neurodegenerative diseases and central nervous system disorders, today announced the successful completion of a EUR 1,100,000.19 fundraising subscribed by two of its existing shareholders, Heights Capital and Invus (the "Fundraising"), to be paid in full in cash. The Fundraising follows a similar structure of shares and warrants, including pre-funded warrants, to the financings conducted in March and October 2026, as further detailed below.

The Fundraising is subject neither to the obligation to publish a prospectus pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 June 2017, as amended (the "Prospectus Regulation"), requiring an approval from the French Financial Markets Authority (Autorité des marchés financiers – the "AMF"), nor to the obligation to publish and file with the AMF a document containing the information set out in Appendix IX of the Prospectus Regulation, in each case for the purpose of the listing on the regulated market of Euronext in Paris ("Euronext Paris") of the Offered Shares, the Pre-Funded Warrant Shares and the Investor Warrant Shares (as defined below) to be issued in the context of the Fundraising.

Use of proceeds

The gross proceeds of the Fundraising amount to EUR 1.1 million, with net proceeds of approximately EUR 1.05 million.

The cash proceeds will be used to finance the Company's operating activities and working capital requirements, in addition to revenues from the early access programs, pending the structural financing of the RECOVER Phase 3 trial.

This financing, supplementing the October 2026 fundraising, covers the near-term funding requirement of up to EUR 2 million disclosed on September 29 and October 7, 2026. This will enable the Company to fund its operations until late March 2027, when the first significant payments related to the preparation of the RECOVER trial fall due. This also remains subject to the number of patients treated under the French named patient early access program (AAC) being in line with the Company's estimates.

The Company's cash flow projections do not assume any exercise of the warrants issued in this Fundraising. If all such warrants were exercised, the Company would receive additional gross proceeds of approximately EUR 0.93 million.

"With this financing, we have completed, on schedule, the approximately €2 million raise we announced with our half-year results," said Jan Eryk Umiastowski, Chief Financial Officer of GenSight Biologics. "We are grateful to Invus and Heights, who have been among our most consistent supporters since November 2024, for standing alongside GenSight once again. Their renewed commitment allows us to approach our upcoming interactions with regulatory agencies with confidence, while we continue to make GS010/LUMEVOQ available to patients through early access and prepare a structural financing for the next phase of its development."

Terms and conditions of the Fundraising

The Fundraising was carried out through the issuance, without preferential subscription rights and without a priority subscription period, of:

  1. 4,237,288 ordinary shares (actions ordinaires), with a par value of EUR 0.025 per share of the Company (the "Offered Shares");
  2. 13,157,898 pre-funded warrants (the "Offered Pre-Funded Warrants") giving the right to subscribe for 13,157,898 additional ordinary shares (the "Pre-Funded Warrant Shares"); and
  3. 17,395,186 warrants (the "Offered Investor Warrants") giving the right to subscribe for 8,697,593 additional ordinary shares (the "Investor Warrant Shares").

Investors had the choice to subscribe for two "units" composed of:

  • Offered Shares to which Offered Investor Warrants were attached (the "ABSA"), with one Offered Investor Warrant attached to each Offered Share, or
  • Offered Pre-Funded Warrants to which Offered Investor Warrants were attached (the "Pre-Paid Units"), with one Offered Investor Warrant attached to each Offered Pre-Funded Warrant.

One Offered Pre-Funded Warrant gives the investor the right to subscribe for one Pre-Funded Warrant Share, and two Offered Investor Warrants give the investor the right to subscribe for one Investor Warrant Share.

The Offered Investor Warrants attached to the Offered Shares and to the Offered Pre-Funded Warrants are identical and thus fungible when they are detached from the Offered Shares and the Offered Pre-Funded Warrants, upon issuance. They will not be fungible with the warrants issued in the Company's previous financings.

The Pre-Funded Warrant Shares and the Investor Warrant Shares (together, the "New Shares") are fungible with the Company's existing ordinary shares of EUR 0.025 par value.

The Fundraising was decided on November 19, 2026 by the Chief Executive Officer, pursuant to the delegation of competence granted to her by the Company's board of directors (the "Board of Directors") on November 13, 2026. The Board of Directors acted pursuant to the delegation of competence granted to it under the 19th resolution of the Company's shareholders' meeting held on May 19, 2026 (the "General Meeting"). The ABSA and the Pre-Paid Units were issued in a capital increase with cancellation of shareholders' preferential subscription rights for the benefit of investors within the category of persons defined by the 19th resolution of the General Meeting, in accordance with Article L. 225-138 of the French Commercial Code, to be paid up in cash.

The issue price of one ABSA is EUR 0.0708.

The issue price of one Pre-Paid Unit is EUR 0.0608.

The exercise price of one Offered Investor Warrant is EUR 0.04565, i.e. EUR 0.0913 per Investor Warrant Share.

The exercise price of one Offered Pre-Funded Warrant is EUR 0.01 per Pre-Funded Warrant Share.

The EUR 0.0708 issue price of one ABSA represents a facial discount of 7% (i.e. EUR 0.0053) to the last closing price of the Company's shares on Euronext Paris on November 19, 2026, i.e. EUR 0.0761 (the "Closing Price").

The exercise price of two Offered Investor Warrants represents a 20% premium to the Closing Price.

The issue price of two ABSA, less twice the EUR 0.0109 theoretical value of one Offered Investor Warrant1, plus the exercise price per share of such Offered Investor Warrants, represents an average subscription price of EUR 0.0704 for each of the three New Shares issued (the two Offered Shares and the Investor Warrant Share), above the Closing Price less the maximum facial discount of 20% provided for in the 19th resolution of the General Meeting.

The same applies to the Pre-Paid Units.

The Offered Pre-Funded Warrants may be exercised at any time within 60 months of their issuance. The Offered Investor Warrants may be exercised at any time within 60 months of their issuance.

In the event all Offered Investor Warrants and all Offered Pre-Funded Warrants are exercised, their exercise would generate additional gross proceeds of EUR 925,669.22 (i.e. EUR 131,578.98 for the Pre-Funded Warrant Shares and EUR 794,090.24 for the Investor Warrant Shares).

Impact of the Fundraising on the Company's shareholding

Following the issuance of the Offered Shares, the Company's total share capital will be EUR 6,261,365.45 (composed of 250,454,618 ordinary shares). If all the Offered Pre-Funded Warrants are exercised, and thus all the Pre-Funded Warrant Shares issued, the Company's total share capital will be EUR 6,590,312.90 (composed of 263,612,516 ordinary shares). If all the Offered Investor Warrants are exercised, and thus all the Investor Warrant Shares issued, the Company's total share capital will be EUR 6,807,752.73 (composed of 272,310,109 ordinary shares).

  • the press releases issued on October 8, 2026 and October 16, 2026 relating to the EUR 1.0 million fundraising,

Risk factors

The Company draws the attention of the public to the risk factors relating to the Company and its business described in its 2025 Universal Registration Document, which is available free of charge on the Company's website (https://www.gensight-biologics.com/).

In addition, the main risks specific to securities are as follows:

  • The existing shareholders who do not participate in the Fundraising will see their shareholding in the share capital of GenSight diluted, and this shareholding may also be further diluted in the event of the exercise of the Offered Investor Warrants, as well as in the event of new securities transactions.
  • The volatility and liquidity of GenSight shares could fluctuate significantly. The market price of the Company's shares may fluctuate and fall below the subscription price of the shares issued in the context of the Fundraising. The sale of Company shares may occur on the secondary market, after the Fundraising, and have a negative impact on the Company share price.

About GenSight Biologics S.A.

GenSight Biologics S.A. is a clinical-stage biopharma company focused on developing and commercializing innovative gene therapies for retinal neurodegenerative diseases and central nervous system disorders. GenSight Biologics' pipeline leverages two core technology platforms, the Mitochondrial Targeting Sequence (MTS) and optogenetics, to help preserve or restore vision in patients suffering from blinding retinal diseases. GenSight Biologics' lead product candidate, GS010 (lenadogene nolparvovec), is in Phase 3 in Leber Hereditary Optic Neuropathy (LHON), a rare mitochondrial disease that leads to irreversible blindness in teens and young adults. GS010 is currently in clinical development, has not to date been granted marketing authorization in France or any other jurisdiction, and is therefore not available commercially. Using its gene therapy-based approach, GenSight Biologics' product candidates are designed to be administered in a single treatment to each eye by intravitreal injection to offer patients a sustainable functional visual recovery.

data.title: U.S. Treasury Yields Fall as Investors Seek Safe-Haven Assets
data.description:
By Miriam Mukuru

U.S. Treasury yields dropped in Asian trade on Friday as risk-off sentiment continued to drive demand for safe-haven assets.

The two-year Treasury yield fell 5.5 basis points to 4.724%, while the 10-year yield dropped 4.4 bps to 5.008%, according to Tradeweb. Twenty-year Treasury yields declined 3.2 bps to 5.419%.

A record initial public offering by Anthropic, which raised $81 billion, failed to revive appetite for artificial-intelligence stocks. Investors continued to question whether the enormous investments in the AI industry would pay off given the rising public resistance toward the industry.

"The blockbuster debut [IPO] couldn't sweep those worries under the rug," Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote, said in a note.

High borrowing costs also raise concerns about the AI companies' ability to continue raising funds to finance their massive expansion.

"The scale of the Democratic win in the midterm [elections] has deepened worry that policymakers could push for slower data-center spending," David Groman, global equity strategist at Citi, said in a note.

The concerns about the tech and AI sector are driving the flight to safety, causing government bond yields to drop, Groman said.

Write to Miriam Mukuru at miriam.mukuru@wsj.com

data.title: Tosca's 2026 Sustainability Report Makes the Case for Packaging as Critical Supply Chain Infrastructure
data.description:
BRUSSELS, BE / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / Tosca, a global leader in reusable packaging and pooling solutions, has released its 2026 Sustainability Report, calling for a shift in how businesses evaluate transport packaging: from a purchased commodity to a strategic component of supply chain infrastructure.

As food supply chains become more automated and face mounting cost and regulatory pressures, packaging decisions increasingly influence operational performance. The report examines how reusable packaging can reduce food loss, labor requirements and transportation inefficiencies while documenting Tosca's progress toward its global sustainability goals.

"Companies invest significant resources in optimizing equipment, labor and transportation, yet packaging is still too often evaluated primarily on unit price," said Eric Frank, CEO of Tosca. "That approach overlooks its role in keeping automated lines running, protecting products and moving goods efficiently. Packaging is an operational input and should be evaluated with the same discipline as the infrastructure around it."

Measuring the Impact Beyond Packaging Waste

The report highlights how reusable packaging and pooling systems deliver measurable benefits across customer operations. For example,

  • Less product damage and food waste: Strong, rigid crates protect products during handling and transport, reducing damage to fresh produce by an average of 6-9%. For eggs, Tosca's reusable packaging reduces damage by more than 50%.
  • Lower labor requirements: Retail-ready reusable packaging saves 307 labor hours per 100,000 crates compared to corrugated packaging.
  • More efficient transportation: Improved load utilization and fewer journeys can reduce transportation costs by up to 25%, alongside associated emission reductions.
  • Less single-use packaging waste: Tosca's reusable packaging solutions have removed 2.229 million metric tons of corrugated packaging from supply chains, eliminating the associated recycling and disposal requirements.

Advancing Global Sustainability Goals

Tosca reported solid progress in reducing the environmental footprint of its own operations:

  • 30% reduction in global Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions intensity per operating hour since 2021.
  • 46% of global electricity sourced from renewables in 2025, up from 33% in 2022.
  • 41% reduction in total waste generated compared with 2024.

The report also highlights Tosca's investments in circular infrastructure, including the CP 1208 Circular Pallet, developed from 100% recycled plastic, and expanded RFID-enabled asset tracking to improve supply chain visibility.

Following its first Double Materiality Assessment and formal climate risk assessment in 2025, Tosca updated its sustainability strategy through 2030, targeting 42% reductions in absolute Scope 1 and 2 emissions and Scope 3 emissions against their respective baselines.

"Reducing the footprint of a packaging material is only part of the equation," said Karin Witton, Ph.D., Global Head of Sustainability at Tosca. "We also have to account for the food lost, transportation required and resources consumed throughout the supply chain. Measuring these impacts together helps businesses identify where the greatest environmental and operational improvements can be made."

Download Tosca's 2026 Sustainability Report

About Tosca

Tosca is a global leader in reusable plastic packaging and pooling solutions, helping businesses eliminate waste and improve supply chain performance. Through its reusable containers, pallets, bulk packaging, and end-to-end pooling services, Tosca helps customers protect products, improve operational efficiency, and reduce environmental impact. Serving customers across more than 60 countries, Tosca is committed to advancing circular supply chains and eliminating waste at every turn.

For more information, visit www.toscaltd.com.

data.title: FRO – Third Quarter and Nine Months 2026 Results
data.description:
FRONTLINE PLC REPORTS RESULTS FOR THE THIRD QUARTER ENDED SEPTEMBER 30, 2026

Frontline plc (the “Company”, “Frontline”, “we,” “us,” or “our”), today reported unaudited results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026:

Highlights

  • Profit of $641.4 million, or $2.88 per share for the third quarter of 2026 and adjusted profit1 of $530.9 million for the third quarter of 2026, or $2.38 per share.
  • Declared a cash dividend of $2.38 per share for the third quarter of 2026.
  • Reported revenues of $921.3 million for the third quarter of 2026.
  • Achieved average daily spot time charter equivalent earnings ("TCEs")2 for VLCCs, Suezmax tankers and LR2/Aframax tankers in the third quarter of 2026 of $148,500, $102,500 and $67,800 per day, respectively.
  • Sold two VLCCs built in 2017 for a total sales price of $270.0 million. The transactions generated net cash proceeds of $179.0 million, which were returned to the shareholders through the payment of a special one-time dividend of $0.80 per share in September 2026.
  • Entered into a three-year time charter-out agreement for one Suezmax tanker, built in 2016, at a rate of $80,000 per day, which commenced in October 2026.
  • Entered into a new senior secured revolving reducing credit facility in an amount of up to $731.8 million in November 2026 to refinance the $1,286.0 million secured revolving reducing credit facility, further reducing the Company’s weighted average interest rate margin to 118 bps as of the date of this report.

Lars H. Barstad, Chief Executive Officer of Frontline Management AS, commented:

“The third quarter of 2026 was defined by the escalation in the Middle East, logistical challenges and time-consuming trading patterns. Utilization has since reached extraordinary levels, and freight rates have moved to all-time highs, with asset values following and the entire tanker complex benefiting. As we are well into the fourth quarter of the year, our bookings so far are at the highest levels we have ever recorded across all three of our segments. With the majority of our spot days already fixed, Frontline is positioned to deliver its strongest result ever, both for the fourth quarter and for the full year 2026. The nine months that have passed in 2026 is likely to change the oil trading patterns considerably in the future, making us optimistic for Frontline’s earnings capacity in the years to come.”

Inger M. Klemp, Chief Financial Officer of Frontline Management AS, added:

“From June to November 2026 we reduced our financing costs through a combination of margin reductions on existing facilities for their remaining tenors and full refinancing of selected facilities, contributing to a reduction in the Company’s weighted average interest rate margin of 60 bps from 178 bps at the end of the first quarter of 2026 to 118 bps as of the date of this report.

We believe that the refinancing of, and amendments to, our existing debt facilities have been achieved on highly attractive terms, further strengthening our liquidity position while reducing our borrowing costs and cash breakeven rates. We continue to focus on maintaining our competitive cost structure, breakeven levels and solid balance sheet to ensure that we are well positioned to generate significant cash flow and create value for our shareholders.”

data.title: Evonik CEO Says BASF Ending Takeover Pursuit Removes Source of Uncertainty
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

Evonik Industries' interim Chief Executive Officer Claus Rettig said BASF's decision to abandon efforts to take over the German chemicals company removes a source of uncertainty for its employees.

"Our plan for the coming years is set. Now we can focus our full energy on Evonik's standalone development," Rettig said. "For our employees, this removes a source of uncertainty."

BASF said Thursday that it would end its pursuit of Evonik after two all-cash offers were rebuffed.

"We are convinced that BASF's derisked all-cash offer of 24 euros per share would have represented significant additional value for Evonik shareholders," BASF Chief Executive  Markus Kamieth said.

The bid valued Evonik at 11.18 billion euros ($12.26 billion), based on share-count data provided by FactSet.
